As a no-cook assembly bowl using ready-to-eat ingredients, the method is entirely suitable, foolproof, and fast.

Fix the backend mapping to unsalted cooked shrimp. Alternatively, if standard pre-cooked shrimp genuinely carries this much sodium, switch the ingredient to raw peeled shrimp and add a 3-minute pan-sear step to ensure the printed nutrition panel stays under the limit.
The title and intro accurately reflect the recipe and ingredient profile. The tone is encouraging, correctly highlights the nutritional synergy of the ingredients, and avoids banned health claims.
A highly appealing, colorful, and fresh lunch option that comes together in minutes without turning on the stove.

Fits the 'Soups & Salads' light main tier perfectly as a substantial, protein-forward grain bowl. (Note: the sodium computation misses the mark, but the actual recipe ingredients as written intend to align with the <=500mg target).
Easily completed in 15 minutes. The strategic use of ready-to-eat quinoa pouches and pre-cooked shrimp are fantastic, compliant shortcuts that deliver on the 30-minute promise.

details.summary: This is a stellar recipe that perfectly executes the book's dietary philosophy and 30-minute everyday-ingredient promise. It is flavorful, well-structured, and relies on smart convenience items like ready-to-eat quinoa to ensure a fast, delicious meal without compromising quality.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent and cohesive. Sweet mango, acidic lime, earthy black beans, and a kick from red pepper flakes create a beautifully balanced Caribbean-inspired bowl.
All ingredients are perfectly accounted for in the instructions, and the division of the olive oil between cooking and dressing is handled clearly.

Instructions are thorough and beginner-friendly. Searing instructions provide both a time range (3 to 4 minutes), an action (flipping once), and clear visual doneness cues (pink and opaque throughout).
The recipe aligns perfectly with its stated Caribbean-inspired cuisine style, utilizing mango, black beans, cilantro, lime, and shrimp.
A quick skillet sear is the ideal cooking method for raw shrimp to prevent rubbery textures, and assembling the rest raw/precooked makes for a bright, fresh bowl.

The computed sodium (738 mg) flagged by the system is almost certainly a database artifact pulling a value for saline-treated (STPP) shrimp, as the recipe uses no added salt and specifies no-salt-added beans. Untreated raw shrimp would bring the true sodium down well under the 500mg ceiling. The rest of the macros are perfectly plausible.
The title is highly accurate, and the intro is inviting, descriptive, and free of any banned 'detox' or 'metabolism-boosting' health claims.
This is a highly appealing, colorful, and appetizing recipe with great textural contrast between the soft quinoa, firm beans, juicy mango, and seared shrimp.
Perfectly hits the dual-condition brief: entirely Mediterranean in character, rich in vegetables, legumes, and lean protein, dressed purely in EVOO and lime.
Zero added sugar (sweetness relies entirely on fresh mango) and a fantastic, high-quality complex carbohydrate base (quinoa and black beans) that lands squarely in the 35g sweet spot for a main.
Fits the 'Soups & Salads' light_main tier perfectly. It reads as a substantial main-plate grain bowl with excellent protein (23.5g) and fiber (8.8g) from whole food sources.

A textbook execution of the 30-minute promise. Using a ready-to-eat quinoa pouch avoids the hidden 20-minute grain cook time, and the active prep is fast and straightforward using easily found ingredients.
